Ground tranport is to be included.  Make sure you stay on top of this.  Tons of issues for us and our guests.

reviews.author: imafloridacracker
reviews.title: Everything BUT Paradise...
reviews.text:
We were invited as guests by our hosts on this trip and after we saw the Trip Advisor reviews we were really excited about staying here.

But this is one of the few times in my experience that TA got it very wrong. The Reserve At Paradisus Punta Cana DEFINITELY DOESN'T even come close to any other Travelers' Choice Winners we've stayed at. If there was an award for Travelers' Choice Losers, they would easily win the award.

First, it took us an hour to check in and that may be the norm. When they start serving you drinks on sofas, you realize it may be longer than just walking up and getting your keys. I still don't understand why it had to take so long but in our case they were overly concerned that the paperwork they had on our host's PREPAID all-inclusive fee wasn't correct (even though they had a confirmed AMEX BLACK CARD on file).

It was indicative of the week to come that front-desk personnel showed up at our host's door at 10:30 pm insisting that certain paperwork be signed then and there (again -- they had a confirmed AMEX BLACK CARD on file).

In fairness, management made a very grand gesture when we checked in and told them that a third couple arriving that day were friends of ours. They volunteered to move us to the building they were in. Our host would be in that building immediately and we would be moved after the first day.

Only, they screwed up our room numbers at check in and we were never able to get it corrected during the week, causing numerous delays and service staff who didn't believe us when we gave them the correct room numbers. At one restaurant I was run down by the wait staff on the way out the door, to be confronted by a woman (presumably in accounting or management) insisting that I was not providing the correct information. Eventually I tired of debating with her and simply walked away.

They brag about all the restaurant choices on the property but one concierge we dealt with said you cannot make restaurant reservations beyond tomorrow night. Another concierge asked us what time window we wanted for reservations and we said 7-8. After she said we had to extend that to at least 7-9, she made five days worth of reservations at 9 pm. When one of our friends objected, we found out you can go directly to the restaurant and pretty much get what you want. So much for that concierge service that's talked about so much.

But that doesn't come close to topping the experience at Vento. That was one of the 9 pm reservations originally but we went to another concierge and that concierge had it changed to 7 pm and gave us a reservation card stating same. So imagine our surprise when we show up and present the card. When the hostess checks her records she says we don't have a reservation until 9. When I point out that the card says 7, she stands her ground. I then ask to see the manager and, believe it or not, he (Cesar) says we don't have a reservation until 9. I tried to appeal to his common sense that we didn't create the card that was signed by a concierge, but he wasn't budging. I grabbed the reservation card and told him I wanted to see the property manager. He then watches me go across the hall and get a photocopy of the card made and I guess he panicked because we were promptly seated. A lady named Mildred showed up, identifying herself as the acting property manager, and did all she could to smooth things over, including comping us with some wine. I never got an answer from Cesar or Mildred as to why they just didn't seat us in the first place (they had the room in the restaurant).

On another evening, a member of our party, discouraged that we were still unseated 30 minutes after our reservation time, slipped the hostess at The Grill $20 and we were promptly seated.

When you check in there is a big deal made about 24/7 room service. You might want to think about that first. I ordered Eggs Benedict and its the first time I've ever had a cold poached egg on a cold, sliced bread roll (with absolutely NO Canadian bacon or hollandaise sauce). So unbelievable it was becoming humorous despite the disappointment.

Most of the food experiences were passable, but only if you value quantity over quality. The Reserve is NOT a place for an epicurean experience. The notable exceptions would be Mole (for a good and RELIABLE lunch -- we ate there three times) and Vento (despite the nasty experience the Ossobuco was fabulous) and Passions (which has a $60 pp up charge) for dinner.

Another "Believe It Or Not" experience: They advertise a pillow concierge so we ordered feather pillows to replace the hard as a rock foam pillows. They delivered two feathers and, believe it or not, a FOAM pillow.

If you've always wanted a massage experience that felt like you were in Grand Central Station, then you'll definitely want to try the YHI spa. The lobby noise was so loud in the treatment room I was in that it drowned out the spa music. The technician was good but the experience was not.

There were numerous intermittent problems getting around on the trolleys. Don't believe it for a minute when they tell you they run ever 15 minutes.  We waited 45 minutes on one occasion from a main stopping point at the beach. After getting on-site personnel to make repeated calls one finally showed up. On multiple occasions I witnessed large numbers of people who simply gave up and started walking back to their rooms.

If we thought it was a screwy check-in, checking out was even more fun. When my wife checked out she specifically asked if there was anything else and the response was no. They didn't tell us at the time that we needed a purple pass to present before our bags could be put in the taxi. You can only get the pass by presenting your keys at the checkout desk. These are the standard plastic keys with the card stripe, not some expensive key. Hmmm….

Unfortunately there are a number of other experiences that I haven't detailed because this is already the longest TA review I have ever done, by far. 

This is a beautiful, well maintained property with nice rooms but the staff is many times uninformed, sometimes untrained and in too many cases, indifferent. There were some OUTSTANDING staff members who were anxious to help, always had a smile and prompt to respond, but they were the exception, not the rule.

This IS NOT a place to go to relax. You spend too much of your time uptight about something that service did or did not do.

reviews.author: bugsmomtoo
reviews.title: Pretty, but not so great aside from that...
reviews.text: Returned one week ago.  The good news (for us anyway) is that this was a reward trip, so we weren't paying for it. The resort is very pretty to look at and hopefully the huge amount of seaweed on the beach is just a temporary problem because the sand is very soft.  We had a great bartender at the pool bar and pretty good service on the beach if you tip. Now for the not so great stuff:  Upon arriving at our room (3721), we walked in and were immediately assaulted by a VERY strong musty smell.  I alerted the front desk and they sent someone with some kind of spray and lit some incense, which made the situation more tolerable.  My sister in law was directly above us in 3731 and had the same problem.  Upon arriving home, I have laundered our clothing 3 times and still cannot get the musty smell out.  I'm going to have to send everything to the dry cleaners and hope for the best. The rooms on that side of the resort are dated and strangely laid out.  Others from our company that were in the 1000 numbered rooms on the other side of the resort said their rooms were fine and nicely laid out. Maybe our side was the original and the other rooms were added later?  Definitely need serious remodeling on the one side for sure.  The food at the restaurants is average at best, with, in my opinion, the best being the breakfast buffet.  Played Black Jack at the casino and the dealers do not check for a blackjack when they are showing an ace or face card, thereby letting others split or double down their money when they cannot beat the dealer if he/she has blackjack. Every other casino I've gone to has the dealer  check first.  Our friend played slots and won the 5 coin line and they would only pay him as if he played one coin. We didn't gamble again on our trip. We have traveled many times to the Caribbean and throughout Mexico, and this was our least favorite trip. We will not return to this resort.

reviews.author: Bsteels80
reviews.title: Not the best!!
reviews.text:
I just returned home from staying 5 nights at Paradisus. The place was clean and staff was nice for the most part. A few bad things happened while we were there. #1, my daughters medication was stolen out of our room. They claimed no knowledge of it. Not until a scene was made did they acknowledge it and poof..it magically appeared. Unreal. I went with 6 people and spent a lot of money there at a so called 5 star resort this was not expected. Must have been an employee because nothing else was stolen from the room. Just not what I am used to and will NOT ever be returning. To make things better my insurance company will not cover the medicine again and I will not give her the medication since it has been in someone else's possession. Now I am forced to purchase the medicine for almost $2,000. 
#2- I had 3 rooms and for my family that I traveled with and my rooms were all over the resort and took 24 hours to put us close together. Eventually they worked it out but we had to move out of 2 rooms and waste more time and money tipping the bell hop for a second time.

With that being said, the babysitting service was great. The place was clean and had great views. I hate to give a bad review when some of the employees were great but when something happens like this, they get a "D" in my eyes. Unbelievable!!

reviews.author: SecretAsian16
reviews.title: Poor Service or Lack thereof
reviews.text:
After finding the gem in Aruba, Bucuti & Tara Suites, who set high standards, it is difficult to find a resort that will meet our expectations.  I was going to give Paradisus  3 stars but my experience got worse each day.  It all boils down to service.  It's the minor details that make me happy like having a cold wash cloth while laying out on the beach or a fruit cup in the afternoon or a flag you can use to call a waiter to get drinks.  

We normally research about the resort & island before we go on vacation.  I read the good and bad reviews and decide which is the best one for us.  I understand that everyone will have a different experience but as I read other reviews, I see a pattern with their service.  The only reason we came here is for a wedding.  We can't stay at a different resort or they'll charge $100/person to attend the wedding.

I knew I was going to have a horrible time when we checked in.  They started speaking to us in Spanish.  They assumed we spoke the language because of our last name & to them we look like locals (they actually asked our ethnicity) because she was wondering why we didn't speak Spanish.  It is rude & quiet annoying.  One of my concerns going on vacation is that we don't speak the language if I have an emergency.  My doctor assured me that they speak English.  Yes they do but barely.  There's a handful who speaks English well. I'm not asking for perfect grammar trust me since English is my second language too but I need them to understand my concerns (if I had an emergency). 

My husband wanted to stay at the Royal Service area of the resort since this is our last trip before I give birth.  The Royal Service is where you get your own butler and their welcome lounge serves premium alcohol.  Just an FYI, you don't get premium alcohol anywhere else in the resort even with the "gold" bracelet.  Is it worth the money?  Not in my opinion.   We didn't use our butler except to make dinner reservation & to book a cabana closer to the beach.  He gave us a fruit platter the first night and chocolate covered strawberries on our second night.  As part of their service they can iron your clothes but we never got to experience it.  

The beach area for Royal Service is separated by a rope from the rest of the resort.   There's no staff to get your drink order or assist you with anything you need like when a palm tree branch falls on you.  I was embarrassed & didn't want people to feel sorry for me, so I quickly took off the branch on top of me & moved my chair away from the branch.  Did I mention I'm pregnant?  It took them a few hours before they took away the branch and no one said anything-apologized or check if I was ok.  Oh wait that's right no one was around to check on guests.  I wonder how many branches fall on their guests on a daily basis.  On our 3rd day on the beach, we tried to locate a waiter to get drinks.  Someone took our order at 11:16am and my drink didn't get there until 11:35.  How do I know this?  I told my husband that I needed to get ready for the wedding by noon that's why I kept checking the time.  I had to go back to the room by 11:30 to shower.  He sent me a text at 11:36 saying that my drink is there and the waiter gave me two drinks.

The water is as clean as the Jersey Shore without the needles and garbage floating in the water.  There's a lot of seaweed.  Nothing compares to the pristine water/beach of Aruba & Mexico.  Curaçao is good for snorkeling/diving.  Costa Rica's water is clean but I wasn't thrilled of the black sand.

The grounds are clean and well kept.  The property is huge and everything is far (restaurants/lounge/reception) from the room.  At night, you should bring a flashlight.  It's dark and you can barely see where you need to go.  There's a lot of stray cats in the area, too.

FOOD -  For an all inclusive resort, the food is ok but nothing memorable or spectacular.  The buffet has a good spread for breakfast and lunch.   We tried Rare, Vento and Pallazo (exclusive to Royal Service guests but it has limited choices).  The host tried to get us to stay for breakfast by saying its small portions but better quality and taste.  It's not any better than the buffet.  The steak at Rare is well seasoned.   The seafood in the restaurants are fresh.  I understand why other guests rated Vento below average.  It's a hit or miss depending on what you get.  I ordered the mix greens for appetizer.  It consisted of lettuce, tomato, cucumber with candied walnuts and two slices of apple with orange vinaigrette.  The salad was swimming in dressing and it was average.   My main entree was the grouper and it was good.

SERVICE - Everyone is friendly and nice but no one went above and beyond their duty.   You might not find staff to help you but there are plenty of staff selling vacation plans or timeshare.  They tried to do this in a sneaky way when we checked in.  They told us we have to come back at the lounge at 9am the following day.   I said my husband can go while I sleep.  She asked, "9 am is too early for you?  You're still sleeping at that time?" To which I respond, "Yes, I'm pregnant."  Then it happened...she touched my belly.  Excuse me, do I know you?  Have you heard of personal space?  The second time they tried to force us to attend a "meeting" for a faction plan was on our second day when we were looking for HotelBeds to schedule our return trip to the airport.  They follow you where you are going until you tell them no the nth time.

At the buffet, you will choke on your food before you get your drink.  I'm not sure if they are overwhelmed but if you tell your guest that you'll be back to get more coffee, please remember to come back.  Don't go to other tables and have nothing left for us (the second time around).  They should have their coffee as part of the buffet just like their juice so the guests can help themselves.  For lunch, they forgot to bring my sprite.  I got it after I finished my lunch.  Then he asked do I want another one?  To go? Cause I'm done and you see us leaving.  

ROOM - They need to upgrade the rooms.  In my opinion it's stuck in the 90's or early 2000. You get your own jacuzzi in the room and jets in the shower.  Not a fan of either one especially after seeing a roach in the bathroom.  I start to wonder how clean the bathroom is.  The night I was getting ready for the wedding I saw another roach crawling on the vanity where all our toiletries were located.  I hope I don't bring that home with me.   I understand that it's the Caribbean but I've been to Aruba, Curaçao, St Lucia, Costa Rica and Mexico (Asia and Europe) but never saw a roach in the resort that we stayed at, specifically inside our room.  I saw bugs outside the room but never a roach inside the room.

 It would be nice if their bathroom is separated by a wall-concrete/dry wall not by shutters.  The vent doesn't work well.  The smell can still reach outside the bathroom.

We were told that the mini bar would be replenished daily but we were running low on our 4th day.  I asked our butler if they were supposed to replenish this and he said yes.  He will take care of it.  We checked out and it's still empty. 

 I'm glad we didn't choose this for our destination wedding 2 years ago.  Based on our stay now, it would have been a horrible experience.  We won't be back to Paradisus or the Dominican Republic. .

reviews.author: Isis Abreu
reviews.title: Muy Poco por 1000 dólares la noche
reviews.text:
Sigue siendo un hotel todo incluido aún cuando pagamos casi el triple por una habitación super especial de Family Concerge. Lo que no nos dijeron  que también estaba incluido además de la hermosa foto de la habitación que si cumplió expectativas, el músicon hasta las 11 de la noche; como tampoco sabiamos que los servicios son mejores Vs.  El todo incluido, pero no llega a ser exclusivo ni delicado. Y La comida sigue siendo de resort promedio. 
Si hubiese costado sólo el doble de la tarifa regular, hubiésemos salido con mejor impresión probablemente. Arreglen le el precio!

reviews.author: Patrick	 M
reviews.title: Be Careful
reviews.text: Beautiful location and property. Food was above average, particularly considering the property was sold out. Drinks were outstanding. That's where the compliments end. The front desk and concierge service is horrible. Wife slipped on a freshly mopped marble hall, (beware entire property is slick marble indoors) and fractured her kneecap. Was taken to the on property 24 hour infirmary, which was closed. Requested a wheelchair 4 times. 4 hours later, was informed all 8 on property wheelchairs were in use. (This property has over 700 rooms, and also has a sister property on site). They cheerfully offered me one in 48 hours. Next morning returned to the infirmary, and sent to the hospital. thank God for Domingo, because he not only drove us, but picked us up, and even went to a 3rd Melia property and got a wheelchair. Located on the third floor, the elevator was out of service 5 times. There is a single elevator. There solution was to carry my wife up and down the stairs. Since we checked in on Saturday, accounting was closed, and we did not receive our discount books until Monday afternoon. Cost me $50 for the cart rental at the golf course. Upon checkout, noticed I was charged a room service liquor charge, I didnt make. As well as taking the liberty of contributing $2 to Unicef. Nothing against Unicef, but shouldnt they ask you? Their answer was go wait in line at reception, and have it removed. Never again.

reviews.author: Michael G
reviews.title: Stay somewhere else! Pretty resort, but that's about it.
reviews.text:
It is hard to relax on vacation when you are constantly told that you should be paying more to be on a better one.  The different levels of service are repeatedly shoved in your face.  We paid a good price for all-inclusive services, yet our color of wristband could only be used in certain areas, and we were often told where we couldn’t go, swim, eat, etc.  I can't say that upgrading our service would be worth the large expense, but the hierarchy of the resort was beyond obnoxious. With off-limits restaurants, bars, and beaches, we didn’t have many places we could venture to on the compound and we felt very claustrophobic.  Find somewhere that values your business rather than trying to squeeze every penny out of you! 

Worst of all was the disastrous restaurant situation.  We did not like the food and there was very little awareness of special diets, but that's to be expected at an all-inclusive (beware – the new restaurant Blue Agave is just a renamed version of the old Mole, which has bad ratings on this site).  That aside, the problem was that the hotel is run so poorly we could never get a reservation where and when we requested.  You have to wait in line to sit down at the reservation desk, but even if you do this long before everyone else, as long as you are “standard” all-inclusive it doesn’t make a difference: your reservation will be messed up every day.  This was a daily frustration that did not work out once the entire time (until my 70-year-old mom started crying and shoved a very large tip into someone's hands insisting that they help us).  You can imagine the 90 minutes of stressful hassle before dinner every night.  For example, one night our reservation was set for a time prior to when we were notified of it.  We soon realized that these “reservation errors” were just a ploy to get us to tip a concierge who would come in and seemingly save the day at the last minute.  This whole process felt ridiculous because the restaurants appeared to be empty every night.  Please note we were not alone in this experience – we talked many guests with similar stories who hadn't opted for upgraded service. 

Even if this hotel was perfect, its location leaves much to be desired. Bavaro Beach is congested and has a massive seaweed problem.  Their resolution for this problem is to have crews operate tractors and dump trucks “cleaning up” during the peak swimming hours.  Once you do get out into the water, your swimming area is limited as constant speedboats and parasailing vessels spew gasoline in their wakes.  And say you manage to get past all of this, your relaxation will further be interrupted by beach vendors trying to force you to buy even more things.

reviews.author: MillionmilerNYC
reviews.title: Too much work to get what you paid for... and avoid paying more
reviews.text:
I have traveled over 1M miles and stayed in hundreds of hotels - economy up to super luxury all around the world.  This place gets so much wrong.  I blame the management and the property - most of the front of the house staff seems to try hard to take care of guests.  We told management on multiple occasions what was wrong to no avail.

PROS
- food and beverage quality was acceptable
- short distance from airport
- catamarans and kayaks were in good shape
- lots of security

CONS
- constantly trying to sell more stuff to you, which defeats the all inclusive value proposition 
- had to work hard to get food and beverage
- horrible, horrible beach with mediocre pools
- a less than average property overall (eg stagnated ornamental ponds with no fish and 3rd floor walk up suites)
- multiple restaurants require formal attire
- the loud scooters, golf carts and tractors that seem to be everywhere at all hours

DETAILS
We picked it because of a great experience at the Paradisus in Playa Del Carmen (good property and great management / staff) as well as the reviews on Trip Advisor.  We should have listened to the many families that told us to stay at the Club Med in Punta Cana.

The pain starts as soon as you arrive with upsell after upsell.  The front desk tried to get us to pay more to get the one bedroom master suite we already prepaid before arrival.  We had to take out a laptop and prove what room we reserved with receipts, emails exchanged with staff before arrival and pictures from their website.  To get the room advertised we needed to buy the family concierge package was what we were told.  We gave up and paid more.  Be prepared for hard sell on low value upgrades and timeshares.  Several guests reported the same experience.  Another guest even approached us during check in to warn of this nonsense.

Family concierge is a waste of money.  The exclusive Olio restaurant was empty every time we went by it.  Our concierge took a phone call in the middle of a conversation with us and walked away before finishing with us after we hadn't seen her all day.  The mobile phone provided to reach our concierge always went to voice mail when we used it.

The beach is just terrible.  In 5 hours at the beach you'll be lucky to have 1 waiter bring you a drink and it will be in a crappy paper cup.  Most days we had to climb over 3-4 foot walls of seaweed to get to the water.  We heard the immense amount of seaweed was not normal.  Everyday, almost all day, there are tractors cleaning up seaweed.  We even got the "pleasure" of a front end loader and a dump truck for 3+ hours blocking our access to the water.  200 yards from us sat a giant tractor belching fumes starting at 10am, while waiting for the dump truck to return for the next load of seaweed.  Management should know better and do the grooming before guests hit the beach.  5am - 9am the beach is very empty.

The pools are fine.  Nothing special.  The towels are very worn out.  

Internet is free.  Bad wifi coverage around the property and barely any speed.  Generally less than 500Kbps.  Lots of connection drops.

Our son enjoyed the kids club.  But we figured out that he loved it so much because he got unlimited screen time to play video games there instead of well planned activities, like he had at the Playa Del Carmen property.  We learned after the fact that they played Iron Man (age 13+) and other age inappropriate movies for kids well under 10 years old, which is unacceptable.

The room was less than average for the price.  It was near a path used by staff on gas powered scooters and golf carts from early in the morning until late at night.  It sounded like there was a highway right outside our suite.  Management should know to keep the back of the house away from guests.  And we couldn't get a hot shower at just about any hour of the day.  Turn down service was only 2 out of 5 nights.  We had to chase staff to get the refrig restocked, more towels and the room cleaned just about everyday -- and we had a family concierge.

They tried to charge us for what we prepaid on check out.  Took 3 revisions of the bill to get things right.

reviews.author: Alison A
reviews.title: If you want the room you booked, expect to pay more
reviews.text:
We just returned from 6 days at the Paradisus Palma Real and couldn't be more dissatisfied with our stay.  We booked a Master Bedroom Suite with a Garden view and when we showed up, we were offered a 3rd floor walk up that didn't have the layout or the size of the room we booked in April 2014 and then paid for in August 2014.  After showing us 2 rooms (neither of which were what we booked), I started to take out my laptop to show the email correspondence with the hotel guaranteeing us the room with the balcony we were told the room had, etc.  Miraculously, if we were willing to spend $1,200 more to stay in the family concierge section we could have that room. Not wanting to fight anymore (and figuring we'd take it up with Amex after the fact), we agreed.  Ironically this room was NOT a family concierge room (it had to be set up while we were at dinner that night).  Our family concierge was to help us arrange activities, get us a spot on the beach, set up reservations for dinner, etc. 
Our concierge was almost completely pointless.  She never answered the phone we were given to reach her on.  On our 3rd night there, we were talking to her and she received a phone call and just walked away from us.  My husband lost his patience.  After her boss witnessed this interaction, she became more attentive.  Needless to say it was not worth the $1,200 extra we were forced to pay after an already expensive vacation.
The resort itself is just fine.  The pools are nice (and there are quite a few of them) although not heated and cold.  The grounds are well maintained.  The food is good, but definitely not great.  The Kids Zone was a hit with my son.  
However if you are going for the beach, this is not the hotel for you.  The beach had seaweed all over it and one day we had to endure 4+ hours of a tractor and front end loader cleaning up the seaweed - this should have been done in the early morning, not at 10 a.m. when the beach was full.  You couldn't really even get in the ocean since it was full of seaweed you had to wade through to get to an area where you could actually not feel like you were taking a seaweed bath.
We have emailed the hotel with our issues and haven't heard back.  This isn't surprising however.  
We stayed at the Paradisus La Esmerelda in Playa del Carmen last year and loved it, which is what led us to try another Paradisus hotel but unfortunately not all Paradisus's are the same.  
This hotel needs a lot of work to make it worth the money it charges for you to stay there.  
For anyone who chooses to stay there, beware of the up sell to get the room you booked.

reviews.author: Renata G
reviews.title: Did not have a great experience, quite the opposite
reviews.text:
It took me a while to write this review because I was very disappointed with my vacation.  I traveled to this hotel in July of 2014 with my husband and  2 boys: 5 and 2.  My father in law and his wife joined us at the hotel, and we met them for some meals and some entertainment.  First, the positive:  this is a beautiful hotel, with very well manicured surroundings.  The rooms are also amazing, very well furnished and spacious.  The beds are comfortable and the bathrooms are very clean.   Don't worry about the hotel not being "on the beach".  The majority of "regular" ( not reserve) paradisus rooms also have to take a shuttle to the beach.  The extra fee for the reserve is well worth the beautiful accommodations and crowd avoidance.   Basically, it is just one big hotel, with the reserve being a newer part.      The entertainment is quite good, especially the beach party.   I highly recommend it.  The staff uniforms are immaculate.  They all look very clean and crisp, just great.  The housekeeping was also very good and honest.  As I said, the hotel decor was lovely and tasteful.  The summer prior, we vacationed at The Beaches resort in Negril and had a great time.  I expected another great week where I can spend my time with my family, yet the kids can go to day camp so my husband and I can have some freedom.  
Well, the child care program was not great.  The teachers did not speak good English.  They were not very attentive, and my toddler had several accidents, even though he is potty trained. There were not a lot of age appropriate activities for my 5 year old, and he was bored.  They ask you to pick up your child at noon for lunch.  This limits what excursions you can do as an adult.  They have snacks at the child area, such as fruit and sandwiches for the kids, but they say that they don;t have a full lunch.  If they offer children sandwiches, why can't they offer something the kids will actually eat?  Also, the daycare closes at 7p.m.  So, if you want to enjoy dinner with your husband, you have to hire a babysitter  for $20 per hour ( for two kids).  They have kids activities  in the evening, but those are usually at the times when the adults have dinner ( 8:00p.m.), so we missed most of them.   The one's we came to were never well attended.   Also, it would be better to have these events at the kids wing, instead of the main theater.  
The shuttle ( which is really an extra large golf card with a trailer) is frequent enough, but it can be unpredictable.  Sometimes they go a certain way, and sometimes they don't.  If a driver sees an extra large crowd at a certain location, he may choose to pull up to the back of the building.  When leaving a main lobby, they may choose to bypass the  Reserve all together.  
The bars:  they just don't have any  creative recipes for drinks like they had at The Beaches Resort, and their offerings were quite limited.  They also made the drinks very sweet, with not that much alcohol - which means extra calories for me.  They don't have a good variety of kids friendly juices.  
The restaurants:  they are beautiful with a nice variety.  Our favorite was Fuego.  The open air concept restaurants get quite hot in the summer, especially the Steakhosue grill - it was intolerable.  
The buffet at the Regular Paradisus was very crowded, and we much preferred the Reserve buffet.  The food at the buffet is average, but there were not enough kid friendly choices, such as chicken nuggets, plain spaghetti, french fries, american style.  The chefs are very eager to please, so if you request a certain item, they will make sure they have it the next day.  They also have a nice pizza bar at the pool of the Reserve.  For some reason, they will not deliver pizza or any other food to your cabana at the pool, and you are forced to leave your comfy spot at the pool and to sit at the uncomfortable tables in the sand ( which is the outdoor snack bar area).  If you choose to tip a few dollars, that rule is not enforced.  So, it is money well spent. They allow food at the pool at the Paradisus main pool ( not at Reserve), but at that pool is a lot more crowded.  At the main pool bar they serve fried chicken on the bone, burgers and fried potatoes, not french fries.  The management also does not allow the guests to come to the buffet and bring a full plate back to your room.  They deem you incapable of that task ( may be because some guests get very intoxicated and drop the plates).  In any case, they ask that you call room service instead.  Calling the room service and waiting for your food can take up to 1 hour.  And, to explain to your children as to why they can't have their pizza in their room while watching TV is a challenge.  Well, at least for me.  Well, at least for 1 hour that i have to wait for that pizza to arrive.  
That brings me to the last point, the Service.  This is something that most people rave about.  Well, I did not find it to be so great.  Basically, the service is good, but very insincere.  It is very clear that all the staff members are waiting for the handout.   I don't mind tipping, and even brought $100 in $1 dollar bills.  But tipping is a reward for good service.  Instead, at this hotel it is an expectation, and if you happened not to bring your money with you , you might get an attitude or a disappointed look.  I have seen people handing out $1 dollar bills for every drink they ordered, everywhere they went. That is up to those guests, but the service should be good whether you tip or not.  My preference is to tip my favorite servers at the end of the trip.  In this hotel, if you don't tip them the first time, some will ignore you for the rest of the week.  Even if you ask them for something and this time you have the tip money, they will take your order and never return.  In this hotel the tip becomes a bribe.   You are not allowed to bring food to your cabana, but if you give a few dollars that rule does not pertain to you.   There are no towels after 7p.m. at the pool, but if you give a few dollars, the towels will magically appear.  This is what happened to the Okie - Dokie Pool attendant.    On our first night at the hotel ( we did not know the rules yet), he is looking at me and my children soaking wet looking for towels, and nothing....until $5 magically appears.  
There are no consistency with the rules:  my father in law was told that he cannot have restaurant reservations for more than x number of nights ahead of time.  My husband and I got reservations for every night of the week right away ( For those of you who think I am cheap, I tipped $20 to the concierge that same day, but after the fact).  
They don't give you a straight honest answer:  we asked to have our beer refilled in the mini bar for several night without avail.  All we got were empty promises.  If you are out, you are out.  There is plenty of beer elsewhere, just give us an explanation.  
Everything takes forever.  The drive to a hotel took a really long time, so I was hoping the check in will be quick.  Not so, it took awhile for someone just to approach us, and the process was lengthy as well.  Everyone just knows the minimum that they have to know for their jobs.  And, if you ask them a question, they will call elsewhere or look into a brochure, which is the same thing as you can do  yourself, ten times faster.  
My last night at the hotel I actually got into a screaming match with a night-time buffet supervisor Valentin.  It was over having some food at the pool.  The situation really escalated to a point  where Valentin announced that he does not need his job there, and threw his badge on the floor.  He was actually shouting at me.  The night-time hotel supervisor could not dissolve the situation, and in the morning someone ( I presumed a manager) called me and promised to e-mail me, but that never occurred either.  This just shows me what kind of caliber people they hire here.  During our stay we were approached on several occasions regarding joining Club Melia.  Based on what I experienced on my vacation, I would never do that.  Next year I am taking my money back to Jamaica, man.

reviews.author: Radwa E
reviews.title: Would never go back
reviews.text:
The resort is beautiful. The room is nice. The service is hit or miss. Depending on weather or not you give them a good tip they will be nicer to you. The food, it total hit or miss some amazing meals and some not so amazing. The drinks are soooo watered down or insanely sweet. My husband and I got food poisoning yesterday so we changed our flight to leave a day early.

Sandra was our concierge who helped us most of the time. Also a gal named Lady. They were very nice and helpful but they tried to do the Melia club time share and trying to get you to listen to a 90 minute speech on your vacation is ridiculous. Then Sandra tried to make us feel bad and say she gets points if we go!!! I clearly wasn't interested but she insisted. Listened to 2 min of the presentation and left. Spare yourself!!! She asked everyday to listen to this presentation but I totally kept blowing it off. 

I would never go back to this resort.

reviews.author: Mario0222
reviews.title: Mangelhafter Gäste Service
reviews.text:
Die Homepage des Hotels ist sehr vielversprechend bezüglich Services in allen möglichen Belangen. Leider traf dies in meinem Falle absolut nicht zu und in einigen Gesprächen mit anderen Gästen konnte man von mehreren Seiten dasselbe hören. Einen kurzen Bericht zu den Überbuchungen bei meiner Ankunft hatte ich ja schon gemacht.  So erging es nicht wenigen  Gästen genau so. Nichts desto trotz wurden wir auf andere Anlagen umgebucht. Mit etwas Glück bekamen sie ein Zimmer in einer vergleichbaren Anlage ,bzw. Kategorie. In meinem Falle hatte dies leider nicht zugetroffen und ich landete in einem dunklen Standard Zimmer in der Nebenanlage welche auch zur Melia Gruppe gehört. Nach der ersten unglücklichen Woche in einer Anlage die ich von früher kannte und selbst nie gebucht hätte sollte es die zweite Woche nicht viel besser werden
Derzeit gibt es eine Baustelle im Bereich Strandabschnitt oberhalb der Restaurants Market Grill und Buffet Naos gibt. Dort entsteht  ein neuer  Zimmer / Wohntrakt und gelegentlich ist mit Lärm zu rechnen.( Photos siehe anbei )
 
Wie gesagt meine Bewertung für Service mangelhaft / unbefriedigend bezieht sich auf Gästeservice allgemein.  Als ich endlich nach einer Woche vom Hotel Melia Caribe, wo ich als Ersatz für meine One Bedroom Mastersuite ein abgewohntes Standardzimmer bekommen habe ins Hotel Paradisus Palma Real wechseln durfte, hatte ich bei Hr, Douglas Jonathan(Frontoffice) angefragt ob ich gegen Aufzahlung natürlich ins Royal Service wechseln könnte. Immerhin hatte ich schon ein Woche von meinem Urlaub verloren und in einem Zimmer verbracht welches absolut nicht meinem original gebuchten dem Standard entsprach.

Nach einer kurzen Absprache mit Front Office Manager Adriana Guzmann wurde mir mitgeteilt dass das Royal Service ausgebucht ist und keinerlei Zimmer zur Verfügung stehen. Dies hatte ich akzeptiert und auf meine Anfrage ob  ich gegen Aufzahlung zumindest nur den Royal Service Pool und Strand benützen darf habe ich von Hr. Douglas Jonathan nie eine Antwort erhalten, obwohl er gesagt hat er wird mich sofort verständigen sowie er seinen Supervisor kontaktiert hat. ( so kann man sich natürlich auch Umsatz entgehen lassen)                                                                                                 Ich wollte die zweite Woche einfach nur etwas mehr Ruhe genießen, um die erste Woche in der ich ins Melia Caribe umgebucht worden bin schnell zu vergessen.

Nichts desto trotz meine One Bedroom Mastersuite mit Gartenblick war absolut top und immer sehr sauber gehalten. Wobei ich beim Gartenblick bemerken muss - Gartenblick kann verschiedenes heißen.In meinem Falle haben die Palmwedel meinen kompletten Balkon verdeckt und somit wurde das Zimmer sehr dunkel und na ja Gartenblick waren halt die Palmwedel.(siehe Photos )                                                                                                                                                                   Die Palmwedel sollte man trimmen- somit gäbe es wieder mehr Licht in den Zimmern und einen besseren Ausblick.

Ein anderes Anliegen - wiederum Gäste Service: Eines abends bin ich um Mitternacht aufgewacht da ich auf die Toilette musste, ich machte einen Schritt aus meinem Bett und lag schon flach auf dem Boden. Der Grund dafür - die gesamte Suite stand unter Wasser und wenn ich sage die gesamt Suite dann meine ich wirklich vom Wohnzimmer bis ins Schlafzimmer.
Das kann schon mal passieren und da kann auch das Hotel nichts dafür.Ich hatte die Rezeption angerufen und erklärt  dass die komplette Suite unter Wasser steht. Nach 40 Minuten kam endlich ein Techniker und  als er die Wassermengen sah hatte  er sofort Kontakt mit der Rezeption aufgenommen. Mir wurde mitgeteilt dass ich das Zimmer wechseln muss und sofort jemand von der Rezeption vorbeikommen wird. Also habe ich mittlerweile meine Koffer das dritte mal gepackt und wartete bis ein Bell Boy kam um mir meine neue Zimmernummer mitzuteilen und mit meinem  Gepäck behilflich zu sein. Nach einer Stunde war leider immer noch niemand hier und ich ging selber an die Rezeption um mich nach meiner neuen Zimmer Nummer zu erkundigen.(absolut kein   5 * Service)                                                                                                                                                                               An der Rezeption wurde mir mitgeteilt dass schon längst jemand bei mir sein hätte sollen.(das übliche Vertrösten und nach Entschuldigungen suchen). Nichts desto trotz bekam ich dann endlich ein neues Zimmer . Die Freude trügte , als ich im Badezimmer Licht machte sah ich sofort dass das Zimmer noch nicht einmal ganz fertig gemacht war und im Kühlschrank außer ein paar Wasserflaschen und Bierdosen die außerhalb gekauft wurden, noch von meinen Vorgängern sein mussten. ( siehe Photos )                                                                                                   Nach einem kurzen Anruf an der Rezeption hieß es wieder warten bis ein neues Zimmer lokalisiert werden konnte. Endlich ein neues  Zimmer gefunden, wurde mir mitgeteilt dass dies ein Zimmer in absoluter Ruhelage ist, was ich mir gleich dachte da es in einem der letzten Blöcke lag. ;)                                                        

Dies war dann kurz nach 3.00 Uhr früh und ich durfte meine Koffer endlich wieder auspacken und meine Bettruhe genießen.                                                                                                                                         Dass vor dem Balkon die Durchzugsstraße vom nebenstehenden Hotel ist ( Lkw Lärm- Personal Lärm; ect ), hatte ich gleich in der früh herausgefunden, deshalb waren die Zimmer neben mir oder der gesamte Block mehr oder weniger auf dieser Seite die ganze Woche so gut wie leer.

Ich versucht ein Gespräch mit General Manager Hr. Conrad Bergwerf führen zu dürfen. Hier wurde mir von Hr. Douglas Jonathan  mitgeteilt, dass ein Termin vereinbart werden muss, und  somit hatte ich um einen Termin mit Hr. Bergwerf gebeten. Da ich ja im Urlaub war und keinerlei Zeitzwang hatte, würde ich mich natürlich dem Zeitraster anpassen. Es nur ein Gespräch unter Berufs Kollegen sein. Leider kam auch hier nie eine Rückmeldung trotz nochmaliger Nachfrage vom Frontoffice zurück. 

Die Krönung meines Aufenthaltes aber war dann eines abends als ich Roomservice bestellt hatte.Ich wollte nicht im Restaurant essen und hab mich entschieden im Zimmer mein Abendessen zu nehmen, was ich auch schon mal Tage zuvor tat. Als ich den Roomservice bestellt  hatte und eine Flasche Weißwein dazu haben wollte , der natürlich extra bezahlt werden muss (immerhin eine Flasche Pouilly Fume USD 95.-), wurde mir dies verweigert  bzw. gesagt ich muss diese auf dem Zimmer bar bezahlen. Auf meine Frage warum die Weine die anderen Tage auf die Zimmerrechnung geschrieben wurden , was ja eigentlich normal ist konnte ich keine konkrete Antwort erhalten.
Übrigens die Weinkarte für den Roomservice  ist sehr gut- keine große Auswahl – aber die Weine welche angeboten werden sind absolut top.
Also wiederum die Rezeption kontaktiert , da ich einfach wissen wollte was der genaue Ablauf ist , bzw. eine Antwort haben wollte wieso die Tage zuvor die Weine auf die Zimmerrechnung geschrieben worden sind, wurde mir mitgeteilt, bzw. wurde ich wieder wie schon einige male zuvor vertröstet , dass sich gleich jemand darum kümmern  würde. Leider war auch in diesem Falle nie eine Rückmeldung gekommen und so habe ich mich entschlossen mein Abendessen in einem der Restaurants einzunehmen.
Komischerweise wurde mir am nächsten Tages eine Flasche Champagner angeboten ( welche ich dankend ablehnte)

Ich könnte noch einige  Vorfälle oder Angaben zum Hotel erwähnen die für mich dann teils obwohl negativ , eigentlich schon lustig wurden, werde aber davon Abstand halten.
Ich finde es sehr schade da das Hotel in diverser Media für den „ einzigartigen Gästeservice „ so groß Werbung macht und dies meines Erachtens absolut nicht zutreffend ist. 
Unter anderem auch in dem Wilkommensbrief  auf dem noch der Vorgänger von Hr. Bergwerf angegeben ist.
Paradisus Palma Real …………..to pamper and create an experience you will remember forever. Our main commitment is hat your Paradisus experience touches all your senses. Our staff will accomodate all your needs. Thank you for giving us the privilege of hosting your vacation.
Nichts desto trotz versuchte ich die restlichen Tage der Woche noch so gut wie nur möglich zu genießen.
Kurzerhand habe ich mich an dem Tag meines Check outs entschlossen meinen Flug umzubuchen und noch eine Woche in Punta Cana zu verlängern, nachdem mir ja die erste Woche wegen der Über/Umbuchung in ein Hotel was ich von früher kannte und nie gebucht hätte, entgangen ist und leider auch in meiner zweiten Woche zu viel negative Dinge in dem Hotel wo Service so groß geschrieben wird erlebt hatte.
Mag sein wenn sie den Royal Service buchen, was ich versucht hatte aber leider nicht gelungen ist, dass dann der Service etwas besser ist. Dazu kann ich leider keine Angaben machen.                             Definitiv stimmt dass der erste Blick von den Angestellten immer auf das Armband fällt und dies scheint den großen Unterschied bezüglich Service zu machen.
Fazit  Ich würde dieses Hotel keinem meiner Freunde oder sonst jemanden positive empfehlen. 
In meinem Falle leider alles andere als zufriedenstellend , deshalb die negative Bewertung und die Überlegung ein Schreiben an den CEO der Gruppe weiterzuleiten.

reviews.author: mmga2014
reviews.title: furto no quarto
reviews.text: Tudo ia muito bem, instalações ótimas, comida boa, todos funcionários muito atenciosos, até que...bom, até eu sofrer dois furtos no quarto! E em dias consecutivos! O hotel, como todos, já alerta sobre deixar os pertences no cofre . Sei que o deslize foi meu, mas não esperava que bastava uma distração para levarem nossos objetos de valor. Primeiro coloquei uma corrente de ouro dentro do armário. No dia seguinte quando fui colocá-la vi que tinham furtado. Fiz a queixa como alerta ao hotel sobre a conduta dos funcionários, e como resposta tive um relatório confuso, com os horários e datas erradas, e a conclusão que ninguém entrou no quarto. Ou seja, eu mesma me furtei. Aí, no dia seguinte, saí do quarto de manhã e voltei depois do almoço. Quando chego tem um aviso dizendo que esqueci o cofre aberto, corri para ver e o resultado foi um furto de US$ 1000,00. Fiz a queixa novamente e estou aguardando uma resposta. Fica o alerta, cuidem muito bem dos seus pertences, jamais os esqueçam e não saiam nunca sem conferir se fechou o cofre!!!!

reviews.author: Michael H
reviews.title: If it is too good to be true it very likely is not
reviews.text: If you want a relaxing and stress free holiday do NOT come here. If you want good service, or often any at all, do NOT come here. If you want a clear sea and not to swim amongst heavy seaweed do NOT come here. If you expect your dinner reservations to be kept on time do NOT come here. If you want your room to be made up reliably each day before late afternoon and the turn down service always to happen and items like the telephone to work do NOT stay here. If you expect the shows always to take place at the time stated on the daily activity sheet (rather than an hour earlier on occasion) do NOT come here. If you expect all the barmen to be able to make simple rum base cocktails then do NOT come here. If you expect the main restaurant not to be closed without warning do NOT come here. If you expect Royal Service to be something special (rather than more trouble than it is worth with chaotic check in and an indifferent butler) do NOT come here albeit the very small Royal Service pool does have more comfortable large sunbeds. All in all a disaster due I would think to poor management and inadequate staff training (compounded often by language issues). We also did not appreciate our King size bed actually being 2 (5 foot) queen size beds pushed together to make a ridiculously large bed which also resulted in the various room light switches being very difficult to reach as they were in the middle and one person having no bedside table or light at all. This hotel simply does not deliver on its advertising and I am looking for compensation for the almost daily problems encountered during our 8 days stay and the failure of the hotel to live up to its hyperbole. A not very good meal in Passion is not nearly adequate to make up for our sufferings.

reviews.author: mb7curitiba
reviews.title: Estava no paraíso porém minha experiência foi ruim
reviews.text: O hotel the reserve at paradisus punta cana é na verdade um hotel dentro do paradisus punta cana, uma area reservada com piscina, restaurante, e lobby exclusivo. Estavamos de lua de mel e pensavamos que a melhor parte da viagem seria nossa estadia no the reserve at paradisus, porém devido a inúmeros problemas nossa experiência de viagem foi ruim, apesar de estarmos num lugar espetacular. Tudo começou com o enorme tempo despendido para fazer o check in exclusivo e explicações sobre o hotel (falam ingles ou espanhol, para os brasileiros acaba ficando complicado, apesar de falar ingles), quando chegamos no quarto uma lampada que ficava em cima do balcão da "cozinha" estava pendurado (como estavamos com o consierge ou atendente) ele contatou a manutenção para fazer o reparo... Assim que ele foi embora, decidimos tomar banho e então tivemos problema com a temperatura da agua, além da agua escoar com muita dificuldade, assim formando um bolsão d'agua, então tivemos que pedir manutenção novamente... O problema da temperatura da agua se repetiu durante toda semana, no final descobrimos que tinhamos que ligar as duas torneiras do banheiro antes de ligar o chuveiro para o mesmo estar em boas condições... Fim do primeiro dia, nada de praia nem de piscina(fecha as 7pm). Segundo dia pela manha tinhamos marcado com nosso "consierge" para a visita para conhecer o club melia (como tinha lido inumeras pessoas falando que tinham sido mal atendidas por não ter ido ao tal encontro decidimos ir...) saímos do quarto as 9 e ficamos entretidos até as 13:30 (tomamos café da manha com uma das pessoas que explicavam sobre o club durante uma hora deste periodo) apos foi uma grande enrolação... Enfim até ficamos interessados porém quando pedimos para ler o contrato e o regulamento do club (que   era citado inumeras vezes no contrato, eles não entregaram de forma alguma), tentaram nos enrolar com outro regulamento e quando perdemos a paciência eles nos disseram que só tinham em espanhol, enfim uma grande roubada. Não vale a pena comparecer, o papel do consierge é somente garantir que voce compareça a tal reunião e os beneficios que terá... O stress foi tão grande em minha esposa que ficou com enxaqueca! Fim do segundo dia nada de piscina e praia! Outros problemas que surgiram nos primeiros dias foram falta de sabonete e shampoo, assim demandando tempo para pedir inumeras vezes por isso. Terceiro dia enfim piscina, apos o cafe da manha me deitei em uma cabana e estava cochilando quando escutei hey, hey, um casal de americanos que tinham reservado a tal cabana, acordei atordoado, pedi desculpas e me senti muito mal por toda situação, não sabia que era preciso reservar pois não tinham nos explicado, pois só pensam nos interesses deles e não nos nossos. peguei uma outra cadeira e pronto. Depois fui a piscina e decidi pedir uma bebida quando chego no bar tinha vários americanos se divertindo e esperando pela cerveja que haviam pedido a uns 20 minutos, esperei uns 5 minutos e decidi sair da piscina e pedir diretamente no lado interno do bar. Como naquela noite tinha sido agendado com nosso consierge, atendente, nossa jantar em um restaurante que necessitava de reservas, achamos que estava tudo certo, quando fomos confirmar, nada, ele não tinha reservado, então fomos no buffet, que é muito bom, porém não era o que queriamos. Na noite seguinte quando conseguimos jantar no restaurante desejado, além de ter que esperar, a comida era regular e ainda apos algumas horas passei mal, fiquei preso no quarto por 36 horas, só fui me recuperar completamente cinco dias depois. E eu tomei somente água engarrafada.  O the reserve fica isolado da praia, uns 15 minutos caminhando (existe um transporte a cada 15 minutos durante todo trajeto do hotel a praia) Enfim, o lugar tem muitos pontos positivos, o paisagismo é sensacional, a comida principalmente do the reserve (buffet) excelente, com uma apresentação dos pratos perfeita, o atendimento em geral foi bom, porém com várias exceções. Tivemos uma bela experiência ao assistir dois filmes deitados em camas na praia com céu estrelado. Ganhamos duas massagens de 25 minutos no spa. Todo o resort foi planejado com perfeição, um verdadeiro paraíso! Pena que não permitiram que pudéssemos aproveitar tudo isso com tranquilidade.

reviews.author: kleighfass
reviews.title: Terrible Food, Extremely Rude Staff, Dirty Rooms
reviews.text: The title pretty much says it all. We had Royal service - not worth it. The food is horrible. We stayed at Paradisus in Playa Del Carmen, Mexico, last year and it was wonderful! Not so lucky here. There are a few friendly and helpful staff members, but they are truly few and far between. Many were actually downright rude and assume that Americans can't understand what they are saying in Spanish - well, I speak Spanish, and I understood them. Some people on the beach had drink orders taken, we were simply ignored and several times made to feel as if we were bothering them just for asking for what we had paid for. Our room was not clean - hairs all over the bathroom, including the tub, and stains on the sheets. The only plus was Passion restaurant, which was excellent, and had been excellent at the Mexico resort, as well.  We are not loud, rude, or pushy people, and did nothing to warrant the way we were treated. My suggestion to you - go to the Playa del Carmen, Mexico Paradisus I instead.

reviews.author: dj B
reviews.title: take the good with the bad
reviews.text: Reall nice grounds and friendly staff but the food was terrible. Half the time i thought i was eating cardboard and the choices we're limited. Beach was filled with seaweed so you really couldnt swim without getting tangled up so i was confined to the pool which is a pretty huge pool and actually nice. Drinks were a bit watered down but i was expecting that because its all inclusive. My biggest gripe was with the roach problem they have in the hotel room. I couldnt sleep because i was too busy on roach patrol. Seeing the roach on the wall right next to my bed kept me up, slipper in hand ready for action until i was able to fall asleep in the late am hours. smh!!! Hotel grounds gave me the luxury resort feeling which i enjoyed. They really need to bring they're food up to par with the looks of the hotel and figure the roach problem. The concierge did not let my cab leave and made me wait 15 minutes to verify if i was checked out and didn't take my word for it and this almost made me miss my flight home. Sad thing is the hotel is actually nice and pretty much all the workers are accomodating. i would go back if you guys fix the issues

reviews.author: Roy H
reviews.title: Careful of Mold in Room
reviews.text:
I am a long term visitor to Palma Real, having bought club membership there in 2006.  This year and last we experienced a problem with mold in the room.  My wife is very allergic and immediately noticed the musty smell.  We noted the problem to the concierge who sent maintenance out to "fix the problem".  The maintenance man looked at the filter, pronounced it OK and told us to keep the air conditioner set at 60 degrees day and night.  Even the chilly room did not change the smell and we were moved after two days.  If you have an allergy problem, please insist on checking the room before moving in as a mid vacation room change is not exactly relaxing.

We also had problems with the pool.  They allow babies and toddlers wearing regular diapers or sometimes no diaper to use the pools which results in a sanitation issue.  On on more than one occasion pools were shut down when guests found diapers or feces in the pool.  I was told that resort rules requires children in diapers to wear waterproof pampers, but no one enforces the rule.

On the bright side was Jose Rivera, captain, in the Naos Restaurant (temporarily relocated to the Bana restaurant due to reconstruction after the fire).  Jose met us at the door each morning with a bright smile and welcome, made sure my wife had a special smoothie every day, and arranged for a special birthday cake for me on his day off.  Jose is truly one of the best.

reviews.author: xkittix
reviews.title: Upgrade to Royal Service, Or Get Terrible Service!
reviews.text:
I'm giving this place a 2 because it's beautiful, the beach is beautiful, it's clean and the food was sometimes good.

However - I will start with the fact that I was hosting my destination wedding guests here and thus we had 20 rooms booked. We ALL had the same exact experience - you have to make reservations and only the people with a butler in Royal Service were able to make reservations. Don't be fooled, the restaurants are NOT booked. When we went, we were able to tip the host and get inside and found the restaurants to be EMPTY. Night. After. Night. Don't tell me so many people made reservations and just didn't show? That would be a lie. The fact that we paid so much money, brought in so many guests, and couldn't get reservations was ABSURD. And I'm not talking about big group reservations, sometimes we'd ask for 2 or 4 and we couldn't get anything anywhere. It was AWFUL.

To top it off, the Naos Buffet was shut down because of a fire. I asked as soon as I heard it happened, months before my departure, and was told not to worry because it wouldn't effect my stay. Lies. They set up some makeshift buffet in the ballrooms and it would move around. Whatever, that didn't bother me. What did bother me was the AWFUL food they served there! The cheese was left out without any ice under it and I am convinced that they reused this cheese at the room service. Anyone who ate cheese was SICK - coming out BOTH ends! My husband lost ELEVEN POUNDS. People were calling it "the Calzone Cleanse" - note: do NOT eat the cheese and do NOT order the calzone from room service. Beyond that, the room service food was awful. The pasta was overcooked and the tomato sauce tasted like ketchup. Disgusting and not what I'd expect from such a high end hotel. But that wouldn't have been so bad if we weren't forced into the buffet and room service night, after night, after night. I got to eat at the Market Grill for lunch once (it was always packed, I quickly understood why) and then we snuck into Bana another night because a friend with a Butler from Royal Service was able to make us reservations (they made them for 8, we ended up with 13, tipped the host $20, and got inside the EMPTY restaurant). 

The service for the restaurants were not the only place where it was a joke. Do not expect a drink from the swimup bar (I mean, you can't carry cash in your bathing suit, so they know you can't tip them). Do not expect service without having tipping-money in your hand first. Do not expect service to the beach. Basically, don't expect anything. I do not blame the workers - they were overworked, underpaid and disgruntled for good reason. If management were to treat them right, give them shorter shifts (I saw people working 16 hour shifts, no joke), and paid them better, maybe they'd be happy to come to work and not miserable. No wonder the service was awful.

This is not just MY complaint - this is TWENTY rooms full of complaints, minus the ones who coughed up the extra dough to stay at Royal Service. 

I am so incredibly disappointed in my stay. HALF my guests getting so sick (two people MISSED the ceremony because they were ON THE TOILET) was my BIGGEST NIGHTMARE for real. If the food was crappy, that would be one thing, but for the people to get sick - I purposely picked this resort because of the lack of reviews of people getting sick.

Some other complaints: the rooms smelled moldy  (which is why there's always incense burning), I saw roaches (disgusting), some of our guests did not get hot water in their showers, and the canopy on the bed fell on one of our guests. I could NOT make this stuff up! One of our guests moved rooms EVERY night because there was always something wrong with it. We were so upset and embarrassed to have our guests pay so much money per night and then receive THIS type of vacation. 

Oh and the resort is very large, so make sure to ask for a room closer to the main area or you'll be walking forever to get anywhere. 

If you're going to come to this resort: (1) Make sure the Naos buffet is open; (2) Upgrade to Royal Service, do not be a fool you'll end up paying tenfold through tips if you don't; and (3) Stay far, far away from the cheese. 

Oh and I'm still waiting for my credit for booking so many rooms. I was supposed to get my room for free and credited back to me... it's been 4 months, STILL WAITING! After that terrible service, food, and everyone getting sick, and the fact that I had TWENTY rooms booked, I can't believe I'm fighting with them for what I was supposed to receive in my contract!!! Terrible company. I'll NEVER stay at a Melia resort again. EVER!

reviews.author: Departure317857
reviews.title: No Tip No Service
reviews.text: The Dominican Republic has developed a snooty attitude over the last few years.  For better service make sure you bring plenty of cash to tip, not just singles!  I personally don't think that tipping on EVERY interaction with a staff member is necessary considering the price tag associated with staying at this property!  Stay at Iberostar.

reviews.author: Holger
reviews.title: Ich habe den Vergleich
reviews.text:
Die Erwartungen waren groß. 
Leider deutlich untererfüllt.
Zunächst die schönen Dinge dieses Hotels:
Strand und Poolanlage, auch die al a carte Restaurants sowie die Zimmer sind schön und luxuriös gestaltet. Getränkeauswahl ebenfalls sehr gut.
Das wars dann auch schon.
Check in dauerte 50 min, und nur vier Paare waren vor uns. Man zeigte mit dem Finger in die Richtung in die wir laufen sollen um aufs Zimmer zu gelangen. Keiner begleitete uns, sodass wir uns in den Anbauten verliefen. Koffer dauerten 60 weitere Minuten.
Das Buffetrestaurant ist eine Frechheit. Klein, steril und gefliest wie eine Kantine. Die Sitzplätze außerhalb sind allerdings schön.
In den a al carte Restaurants war das Essen gut. Zugleich erwarte ich einen deutlich!! besseren Service. Wir wollten 4 Gänge Essen und bestellten als Gang zwei ein Gericht mit Garnelen und als Hauptgericht ein Rinderfiletsetak. Beides war gut, doch trotz deutlicher Bestellung kamen beide Gerichte gleichzeitig. Da saßen wir nun, zu zwei an einem kleinen Tisch und hatten vier große Teller auf dem Tisch. Die Konsequenz: nix passte zusammen und ein Gericht wurde natürlich kalt.
Wäre das nur ein Mal passiert, nun gut. Es ist drei Mal passiert und kann nicht sein.
Wir besuchen regelmäßig das Hotel Iberostar Bavaro, Iberostar Grand Bavaro und Secrets Royal Beach; alle auch am Bavarostrand. Alle drei kann ich deutlich mehr empfehlen!

reviews.author: Matt C
reviews.text: Very beautiful facility. Very nice Beach as well. Beach security does not do a good job w/ keeping locals from soliciting you while you are trying to relax. Waiting staff does not come around very often in beach/pool areas to take orders. Food in resort is average at best. For a Resort in 2014 not to have wifi anywhere but the lobby is unacceptable.

reviews.author: Paddy
reviews.title: Unsatisfied
reviews.text: Although Punta Cana is one my favorite places to visit, my family has traveled there at least 6 times, this resort just didn't hit the mark.  Let's focus on the positive, the staff was incredible, friendly, knowledgeable, very helpful.  The activities folks, waiters, reservation personnel, and excursion services were particularly helpful.  The food was ok, I've come to expect mediocre food, especially in these types of all inclusive resorts.  They had many choices, but nothing really stood out and knocked us over.  This resort tends to milk things a bit, they have several levels of what "all inclusive means"; essentially restricted in where you can go, based on how much you pay and whether you have kids or not (which is reasonable).  My expectation when I travel to this class or resort, I expect full access with no last minute messages such as "you don't have the right color or wrist band for this restaurant", its just frustrating.  This resort is dated, it needs a lot of work just on basic maintenance, which I think can be made if prioritized by the management.  What was was shocking is this resort had a major renovation going on which they don't mention to you in your reservation.  Its an eye sore to say the least and going on right next to the main pool.  It was billed as a renovation but in reality it was necessary due to major fire damage brought on by a fireworks display that went wrong.  The golf course that services this resort was exceptional, but its not free but they bill as such.  The course doesn't bill you a green fee but they do charge a cart fee of $65 per person and in my golfer's book that's a "green fee"; this really turned me off.  The beach view was pretty but the beach gets overrun by seaweed which has to be removed by dump truck.  They try to manage it, but at one point it almost came up to my knees.  Macao Beach, which is public state park up the coast, now that's a beautiful beach, a must see.  Bottom line, for the amount of money, it wasn't worth it, I won't go there again.  I write this, so the hotel can address the issues and improve, but for the time being, if you're investigating a vacation, steer clear of this place.

reviews.author: SAChanning
reviews.title: Royal Service is OVERRATED!
reviews.text:
I'll start by saying that it was a good vacation.  Honestly, there is precious little you can do to truly screw up a beach and palm trees.  And, if not for the grandiose claims of the website, we probably would have never been the wiser.  However, the whole Royal Service stinks of a giant bait and switch.  

When we arrived, we were taken to the Royal Service lounge where we waited for someone to check us in.  We were then told to wait for our butler and that he would show us around the property.  20 minutes later, still with no butler, we were told we could go and just have lunch and then come back.  We did so, returned 45 minutes later, and then had to wait another 20 minutes for the butler to show up.  Off to a bad start.

The rooms feel cheaply finished. The showers are plastic inserts and very difficult to figure out.  The sheets were old and pilling and very uncomfortable.  Being in the royal service, I was expecting at least the quality of bedding that I have at home (and I assure you, our bedding comes from the sales bin at Bed Bath and Beyond).  

Unlike any other "luxury" all-inclusive I have ever visited, this resort refused to provide snacks in the room, and only included lays potato chips or plantain chips.  If you wanted a candy bar or a pack of crackers you had to go to the store and buy them. The cleaning service also never fully cleaned our room after our arrival, which meant that we were taking time on our vacation to clean our own room.  

The butler service is largely useless.  Our butler forgot to make us dinner reservations on two of the five nights and did not seem to get us "preferential" reservations.  In fact, one night he told us that the restaurant we wanted to go to could only get us in at 7:30 (we wanted 8:30).  We showed up at 7:30 and the restaurant was 3/4 empty.  By the time we left at 9 it was still 3/4 empty, and had never filled up.  

The pool concierge is even more useless.  The only way we could guarantee a reserved bali bed up by the water was to tip an extra amount each day.  Per the resort's website, the royal service pool benefits provide the following: (i) Private pool for adults only, (ii) Pool concierge, (iii) Fresh fruit and juice service, (iv) Selection of top brand sun creams, (v) Refreshing water spray, (vi) Aromatic cold towels, (vii) Sunglass cleaning service, (viii) Drinks service, (ix) Newspapers, magazines and books, (x) Board games and playing cards.  Going through the list one at a time, the pool was private.  I am not sure what a pool concierge is but I am pretty sure we never saw one.  There was fresh fruit and juice service, and the guy came around to offer it around 1 time per day.  THERE IS NO SELECTION OF TOP BRAND SUNSCREENS.  This was easily the most frustrating portion of the trip, as the only sunscreen available was a watered down jug of generic sunscreen (watered down to the point where it wouldn't even stay on the skin).  Had they told us this, we would have brought our own sunscreen from home.  Instead, we had to buy it from the shop there at a 3x markup over the states.  I don't know what a refreshing water spray is, but I am pretty sure we never saw it or had it offered during the course of our stay.  There were no aromatic cold towels - just towels that expanded a little when dunked in water.  Nobody came around to clean sunglasses the entire week we were there.  The drink service would come to us once a day, other than that we had to go and wait 15 minutes at the bar for someone to make us a drink.  There was a photocopy of a newspaper from Miami, but the only books they had were books left by previous guests - all of which were in terrible condition (there were no magazines).  Every time my wife asked about playing cards we were told they didn't have any.  

In case you can't tell, we felt duped by the Royal Service.  Yes, these are all incredible luxuries.  However, we decided to pay the marked up royal service fee to try and take advantage of the luxuries, and felt like there was a bait and switch.  When I went to complain to the head of the Royal Service, he couldn't be bothered to get off the phone or take my information.  Instead he begrudgingly gave me a bottle of 50 SPF sunscreen (I asked for something lower for my wife - but was told they had nothing else) and then summarily ignored again.  

All that said, I did give the resort a 2/5 because the dinner restaurants were very good.  If you can stay away from the buffets (which the butlers push hard) the food is well done.  We did get convinced to do dinner on the beach at the show one night - and that was awful.  Every buffet item was terrible.  However, the restaurants were good at dinner time.  

However, I would STRONGLY suggest looking elsewhere.  You can do better!  Don't waste your money here.

reviews.author: Ruddy G
reviews.title: No vale la pena
reviews.text:
La comida no es buena, el personal ofrece un trato indiferente, las instalaciones no tienen nada especial, el wifi es inestable y de mala calidad, el room service dura mas de una hora en llegar, la playa es buena como la mayoría de la isla.

No vale la pena, hay mejores opciones a igual o menor precio.

reviews.author: The L
reviews.title: Warning to Brides!!
reviews.text:
So we are coming up on our one year anniversary and i am only now able to bring myself to write a review. I still can't even look at the wedding photos without crying. 

Deep breath: here's how it all went down.

After months of emailing back and fourth i get down there and NOTHING is set. I have a meeting and go over EVERYTHING i thought was alreay worked out. After a series of arguments with a very rude romance planner i sat down and again explained that i wanted white wild flowers with green sprigs in all of the bouquets. She says she will give me plain white roses and they want to charge me through the nose for special boquets even though this comes standard with the package. Eventualy she agrees to do white with sprigs of green, no idea why this is an issue in the first place. On the day of the wedding my flowers are pefect. However, all of my bridesmaids have neon green/yellowy roses. They do not fix this. They do charge me. The pictures with bridesmaids now look absurd unless they are in black and white. The black ribbon they used to wrap the wrong flowers got wet waiting in the vases and leaked maroon all over our hands and my white wedding gown which is subsequently ruined. They do nothing about this, not even an apology or offer to clean my destroyed wedding gown. Just hand me and my bridesmaids a bunch of wet cocktail napkins from a nearby bar and hurry us down the aisle. Similarly i wanted white roses with various colored flowers in them on the tables. I say as long as they are mixed colors i don't care what flowers they use except for birds of paradise, which i hate. No birds of paradise please! This is given to them over the phone, in e-mail with photos for clarification and in person. How did the centerpieces turn out? All white roses with three birds of paradise plopped in the middle. Again I am charged through the nose for special flowers. The reception itself, I was assured, would be in an off the beaten path location on the beach. It was instead directly next to the entertainment/main pavillion of the resort, strangers walked into our wedding several times. This was the reception (which all things aside was a blast!!) so it was not as bad as when a man in a speedo tried to walk through my ceremony while my dad and I were prepariong to walk down the aisle. I had to stop my heartfelt father daughter moment with my dad before he gave me away to shout at a man in a speedo, yes the guests heard me. No idea where the staff was who, I was assured, would keep our event private. 

At this point my wedding was running two hours behind because the phone lines went out in the resort and i couldn't get a hold of my romance coordinator to come to the spa and help me with the language barrier. They took 6 hours to paint my nails (they have no dryers so with the heat and humidity they were still wet at the wedding) do my makeup, which was a disaster and my hair which was all wrong. My big soft curls were tiny poodle spirals. I had to rake the curls out smudge up my eyeliner and run (looking like i just got back from the beach basically) to our ride from the reserve to the main resort. The van they had set up was in fact 1 golf cart for my entire bridal party, my girls held my dress over my head while we sped along, further messing my already disastrous hair and maroon hands/dress situation. While my guests waited they had been coralled into the gym where it was air conditioned to stand around in an awkward way breathing in other people's BO. Awesome.         

They front loaded all of the wedding tradtions (father daughter dance, toasts, announcements etc.) into the first 30 minutes of the night, totally ignored our itinerary. Everyone commented on how weird this was. They threw away our cake topper, which my sister spent weeks making for me as her gift and a special wedding keepsake to hopefully pass on to my daughter. Sorry lady, we chucked it! Because of the lateness i got no getting ready photos, or even time with my bridesmaids and very few formal photos as we lost the light. Oh, also, the formal photos were supposed to be taken somewhere away form the reception site, but were in fact taken right next to it as my guests watched, the result is a lot of awkward "someone is watching me" looking photos. 

I did like our photographer. The DJ and light up dance floor were great. Food was good. Weather was perfect. Rooms were gorgeous and we returned on our wedding night to rose petals, champagne and a bubble bath, all a lovely and romantic suprise! Be careful with this place though. In hindsight i should have demended to see a clock at the spa when i felt like it was getting late. I should have demaned that they fix the flowers and compensate me for my dress, cake topper and some of the photos as the session ended up being cut very short. Frankly I assumed with all of the messes they would offer it!! It was my special day, and it was a mess. I was kind of heartbroken and just didn't even think to fight it out.

A few final notes: there is no air conditioning outside of the gym and bedrooms. The WiFi doesn't work outside of the rooms so don't depend on internet messenger apps to communicate with your people. If you book the reserve it will take a lot of time out of your trip traveling to the main resort to see your guests. Also, the guards there will fight with you trying to keep non reserve people out even if it is your bridal party on your freaking wedding day! Yeah, that happened, made my poor mom cry! 

So there you have it. If it wasn't a sunset wedding maybe we could have fixed a lot of this.
